title: The heart's two halves

data.source: RR interval time series from healthy subjects, records 000, 002, 003 and 005 (Irurzun et al. 2021), PhysioNet, doi:10.13026/51yd-d219

prediction: H1: in all four people more than half of beat-to-beat changes are lengthenings, with a 95% interval above 0.5. H2: in all four the median quickening step is the larger. H3: every breathing-band peak lies between 0.18 and 0.33 Hz.
baseline: A time-symmetric rhythm, which gives exactly 0.5 and equal steps; and each record shuffled and played backwards through the same code.
why: All three of the lens's predictions failed as written. Three of the four people did show slightly more lengthening than shortening, but one showed less, the median steps tied in all four, and one breathing peak lay outside the band. What failed is the lens's tidy picture of the breath. CRR does not ask the two halves to be equal on the clock, so this does not bear on it either way. And the heart cannot show a pause between breaths at all.
claim_kind: prediction (about the lens's picture of the breath, not about CRR)

alternatives.forks: Other readings of "more beats slowing": zero changes counted half, 3 of 4 people; longer runs of slowing, 3 of 4; larger mean quickening step, 3 of 4. None gives 4 of 4.

operating_characteristics: With about 60000 changes a person a share of 0.51 would be told from 0.5 nearly every time, so the failure is informative about the lens's picture. A pass would have been "partly" at most.
second_check: Adapted and re-run by a worker who did not write the mapping. No person has reviewed it.
